steps.title: Assess CKD stage and labs
steps.body: Monitor calcium, phosphate, PTH, and vitamin D. Abnormalities worsen as GFR declines — begin surveillance at CKD stage 3.
steps.tip: Trend labs every 3–6 months in stage 3–4, more often in stage 5.

steps.title: Dietary phosphate restriction
steps.body: Limit high-phosphate foods and processed additives. Diet is first-line before escalating binders.
steps.tip: Protein needs must be balanced — involve renal dietitian.

steps.title: Phosphate binders
steps.body: Calcium-based binders (with meals) or non-calcium binders (sevelamer, lanthanum) when hyperphosphatemia persists.
steps.tip: Take binders with meals to bind dietary phosphate.

steps.title: PTH management
steps.body: Secondary hyperparathyroidism: active vitamin D analogs or calcimimetics when PTH exceeds stage-based targets.
steps.tip: Avoid hypercalcemia and adynamic bone disease from over-suppression.

steps.title: Refer for parathyroidectomy
steps.body: Severe persistent hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, or calciphylaxis may need surgical or cinacalcet-based escalation.
steps.tip: CKD stage 4 PTH target often 2–9× upper limit of normal.
